fact: L'Economiste Maghrébin reports that Tunisia presented the outlines (grandes lignes) of its national AI strategy for 2026-2030 at a ministerial council, carried by ICT Minister Sofiane Hemissi; the article is dated 2026-08-17 and gives no adoption or launch decision.
The article says no precise budget, detailed timetable or result indicators for the strategy had been made public, and names no body charged with carrying it out (article dated 2026-08-17).

ICT Minister Sofien Hemissi described the national AI strategy's priority sectors (digital health, agriculture, energy, transport, digital administration) and four axes at an engineers' order conference on 23 May 2026, and said his ministry had begun drafting legal and regulatory frameworks for AI; the report does not say the strategy was adopted or launched.

THD reports the national AI strategy has been in preparation since 2018 and that four ministers signed an MoU on preparing it and its implementation plan on 19 February 2022; as of 22 July 2026 the Official Gazette holds no text instituting or adopting it.

THD reports the steering structures meant to carry the strategy are idle or never created: the digital economy council has had no known meeting since 29 March 2018 and the digital development agency was never set up (article of 22 July 2026).
The chapter lists Tunisia among 13 African countries with AI strategies or draft AI policies as of July 2025, without saying whether Tunisia's was adopted or a draft.
The column says the Ministry of Communication Technologies has been finalising a national AI strategy since November 2024 and its formal adoption is still awaited.
Lawyer Zied El Air says the broad outlines of a national AI strategy for 2026-2030 were presented at a ministerial council in August 2026, as a policy orientation and not a binding text.
ICT minister Sofiane Hmissi said the national AI strategy has been finalised and is in validation within state structures, with hope it is announced soon.

Communication Technologies Minister Sofiane Hemissi told Leaders on 6 February 2025 that Tunisia was finalising a national AI strategy, a first version having been reviewed by Tunisian experts and some 30 diaspora experts and a second to go to wide consultation from mid-February 2025.
